log.text: Light Screen up on P1's side
Light Screen ended on P1's side

decisions.rationale: Lead Klefki + Rotom-Wash: Klefki sets Prankster screens (both Steel resists Fairy, neutering Mega Floette's boosted attacks). Rotom-Wash is Ground-immune via Levitate to blank Garchomp EQ, resists Rock Slide, can burn Garchomp/Scrafty with Will-O-Wisp, and pivots with Volt Switch. Mega Metagross (Jolly 178 outspeeds Garchomp and Mega Floette, OHKOs Floette with Meteor Mash) and Life Orb Dragapult (Shadow Ball/Draco Meteor cleanup) wait in back.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has Mega Floette-Eternal (Floettite, likely Fairy Aura on Mega), Garchomp (Life Orb, Jolly, Rough Skin), Talonflame (Focus Sash, Gale Wings), Milotic (Sitrus Berry, Competitive — avoid Intimidate/Parting Shot into it), Scrafty (Lum Berry, Intimidate), Goodra-Hisui (Leftovers, Sap Sipper). Klefki resists Fairy and Rock; Rotom-Wash immune to Ground via Levitate. Mega Metagross at 178 Speed outruns Garchomp (134-169) and Mega Floette (likely 112-144 range).

decisions.rationale: Lead Mega Floette plus Garchomp for immediate pressure into Dragapult, Incineroar, Metagross, and Rotom-W; retain Talonflame Tailwind and Milotic’s Competitive/Icy Wind as speed-control and Intimidate-punish insurance.
decisions.notebook: Opponent roster is Metagross-Mega, Klefki screens/TWave, Incineroar Intimidate/Fake Out, Life Orb Dragapult, Rotom-W, and Corviknight Tailwind. Preserve Mega Floette to pressure Dragapult and Incineroar; Garchomp pressures Metagross and Rotom-W, while Talonflame and Milotic provide complementary speed control.

decisions.rationale: Reflect (Prankster +1 priority) goes up before any foe move, reducing Garchomp's Life Orb Earthquake into Klefki from 66-95% to ~44-63%. Rotom-Wash then burns Garchomp with Will-O-Wisp, permanently halving its Attack and providing chip. Rotom is immune to EQ via Levitate, and Klefki 4x resists Floette's Fairy moves, so the opponent cannot easily punish this line. Burn + Reflect neuters their primary physical breaker for the rest of the game.
decisions.notebook: Opponent: Mega Floette-Eternal (Floettite, Fairy Aura on Mega, 155 SpA), Garchomp (Life Orb Jolly Rough Skin), Talonflame (Focus Sash Gale Wings), Milotic (Sitrus Competitive), Scrafty (Lum Intimidate), Goodra-Hisui (Leftovers Sap Sipper). Klefki 4x resists Fairy; Rotom immune to Ground via Levitate. Mega Metagross at 178 Speed outruns Garchomp (134-169) and Mega Floette (109-169). Priority: Reflect turn 1 to neuter Garchomp EQ.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolve and apply immediate high-pressure damage to Rotom-Wash while Garchomp targets Klefki with its strongest single-target Ground option, aiming to deny screens and force favorable early trades.
decisions.notebook: Opponent roster plan: respect Klefki Prankster screens/TWave, Mega Metagross, Incineroar disruption, Life Orb Dragapult, Rotom-Wash, and Corviknight Tailwind. Mega Floette is an important Fairy Aura win condition versus Dragapult and Incineroar; preserve Talonflame and Milotic for speed control and Fire/Water coverage.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Rotom-Wash)
decisions.rationale: Light Screen goes up at Prankster +1 priority before any foe move, giving both screens. Rotom Protect avoids the guaranteed Energy Ball KO. Klefki is almost certainly KO'd by Garchomp EQ (44.5–63.4% into 40% HP) but dies having set both screens for 8 turns. This gives a free switch to full-HP Metagross, which with Reflect+Light Screen can Mega Evolve and outspeed both foes at 178 Speed. Rotom survives at 17% + Leftovers recovery, preserving a pivot.
decisions.notebook: Both screens (Reflect + Light Screen) active with Light Clay for 8-turn duration. Mega Metagross at 178 Speed outspeeds Garchomp (134–169) and Mega Floette (122–154). Rotom-Wash is a valuable pivot with Volt Switch; preserve it. Opponent has Talonflame (Gale Wings, Focus Sash), Milotic (Competitive, Sitrus), Scrafty (Intimidate, Lum), Goodra-Hisui (Sap Sipper, Leftovers) unrevealed in this game; only 2 of the 4 are brought.

decisions.rationale: Metagross-Mega (178 Speed after Mega Evolving) outspeeds both Floette-Mega (122–154) and Garchomp (134–169). Tough Claws-boosted Meteor Mash has a high OHKO chance on Floette-Mega (≈99–185% range). Metagross-Mega also takes hits well behind Reflect+Light Screen: Garchomp Earthquake ≈40–58%, Floette Moonblast ≈26–37%. Dragapult would be OHKOed by Floette Moonblast (116–162%) even through Light Screen, making it a poor switch-in. Rotom must stay in; its move will be decided next.
decisions.notebook: Screens (Reflect 7t, Light Screen 8t) active with Light Clay. Metagross-Mega at 178 Speed outspeeds both current foes. Tough Claws Meteor Mash threatens Floette-Mega with OHKO; Bullet Punch is a priority fallback. Garchomp EQ does 40–58% to Mega Metagross behind Reflect. Rotom-Wash is low (22%) but immune to Ground. Opponent has 2 of {Talonflame, Milotic, Scrafty, Goodra-Hisui} unrevealed. Dragapult is frail vs Fairy and should be preserved for later.

decisions.rationale: Energy Ball cleanly pressures the weakened Rotom-Wash while Stomping Tantrum targets the weakened Klefki for a likely double knockout without damaging Floette-Mega.
decisions.notebook: Klefki is Light Clay Prankster with Reflect, Light Screen, Thunder Wave, and Dazzling Gleam. Rotom-Wash is Leftovers Levitate with Hydro Pump, Volt Switch, Will-O-Wisp, and Protect. Preserve Mega Floette as the Fairy Aura answer to Dragapult and Incineroar; retain Talonflame and Milotic for speed control and coverage.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolve Metagross to reach 178 Speed, outspeeding both foes. Tough Claws-boosted Meteor Mash into Floette-Mega has ~99-185% range, very likely OHKO, removing the Fairy-type threat before it can KO Rotom-Wash with Energy Ball. Rotom-Wash uses Will-O-Wisp on Garchomp; even though Garchomp moves before Rotom, the 85% burn chance permanently cripples its physical attacks for the remainder of the game. If Meteor Mash low-rolls and Floette survives, it likely KOs Rotom, but burned Garchomp is manageable with Mega Metagross + Dragapult in back.
decisions.notebook: Klefki fainted after setting Reflect (Light Clay) and Light Screen. Screens have ~6-7 turns remaining. Metagross-Mega at 178 Speed is our fast mode. Dragapult preserved in back. Opponent has 2 unrevealed from {Talonflame, Milotic, Scrafty, Goodra-Hisui}. Garchomp Life Orb + Rough Skin confirmed. Floette-Mega is their special wallbreaker with Fairy Aura. Burn on Garchomp is high priority for long-term game control.

decisions.rationale: Protect Mega Floette from Mega Metagross's potentially lethal Meteor Mash while Garchomp chips Metagross through Reflect; preserving Floette is especially valuable against the unrevealed back Pokémon.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Mega Floette as the primary Fairy Aura answer to Dragapult and Incineroar. Talonflame supplies Tailwind with Focus Sash intact; Milotic provides Icy Wind speed control and benefits from opposing Intimidate.

decisions.rationale: Meteor Mash OHKOs Floette-Mega if it stays in (102.8-193.3%). Volt Switch into the same slot covers a switch: if Floette switches to Talonflame, Meteor Mash (29-55%) breaks Sash and Volt Switch (45-88%) likely KOs; into Milotic, combined damage is strong and Rotom pivots to Dragapult. If Floette Protects (1/3 success after last-turn use), both moves are blocked but we lose nothing critical. The only soft outcome is a Goodra-Hisui switch-in, where both moves are resisted, but Rotom still escapes to Dragapult and Metagross survives Garchomp's burned EQ comfortably behind Reflect. This line removes or severely damages their Mega while preserving Rotom via pivot.
decisions.notebook: Opponent team: Floette-Mega (Fairy Aura, Modest, Floettite), Garchomp (Rough Skin, Life Orb, Jolly, burned), plus 2 of {Talonflame Focus Sash Gale Wings, Milotic Sitrus Berry Competitive, Scrafty Lum Berry Intimidate, Goodra-Hisui Leftovers Sap Sipper}. Screens from Light Clay Klefki still active for several turns. Dragapult (Life Orb, Timid, 213 Speed) preserved full HP in back. Metagross-Mega is our primary win condition under screens; removing Floette-Mega is the top priority. Garchomp burned and heavily nerfed by burn+Reflect. Opponent likely to switch Floette to preserve it; Talonflame is the most dangerous switch-in due to Fire STAB into Metagross.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.
Switching Floette preserves the essential Dragapult/Incineroar answer from Meteor Mash; Garchomp pressures Metagross into a much more manageable range without damaging Talonflame.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Metagross-Mega is Jolly with Meteor Mash, Zen Headbutt, Bullet Punch, and Protect; Rotom-Wash has Hydro Pump, Volt Switch, Will-O-Wisp, and Protect. Preserve Mega Floette for Dragapult and Incineroar where possible; Talonflame's intact Focus Sash and Tailwind are key tempo tools.

decisions.rationale: Milotic gives the safest endgame into the revealed Dragapult and critically low Metagross while preserving Mega Floette for later matchup value.
decisions.notebook: Dragapult is Timid Life Orb with Shadow Ball, Draco Meteor, U-turn, and Protect. Metagross-Mega is Jolly with Meteor Mash, Zen Headbutt, Bullet Punch, and Protect. Rotom-Wash has Hydro Pump, Volt Switch, Will-O-Wisp, and Protect; Klefki established dual screens with Light Clay.

decisions.rationale: Dragapult (213 Speed) and Metagross (178) both outspeed Garchomp (134–169). Draco Meteor is a guaranteed OHKO on the 49% burned Garchomp before it can Earthquake, so Metagross survives. Zen Headbutt into Milotic deals 40–75% and pressures the healthy Milotic while Garchomp is removed. If Garchomp Protects, Metagross still lives, Milotic is chunked, and only Dragapult takes an Ice Beam; the -2 SpA is manageable with U-turn pivot potential. Preserving Metagross is critical because Bullet Punch threatens Floette-Mega (46–89%) for the endgame.
decisions.notebook: Opponent team: Floette-Mega (Fairy Aura, Modest, Floettite), Garchomp (Rough Skin, Life Orb, Jolly, burned), Milotic (Sitrus Berry, Competitive, Bold), Talonflame (Focus Sash, Gale Wings, Jolly, fainted). Screens from Light Clay Klefki still active several turns. Metagross-Mega is primary win condition under screens; Bullet Punch does 46–89% to Floette-Mega. Dragapult (Life Orb, Timid, 213 Speed) is fastest on field. Rotom-Wash (28%) is only bench. Garchomp burned and Reflect-nerfed; Draco Meteor OHKOs it. Floette-Mega is the opponent's main threat; removing it wins the game.

decisions.rationale: Protect Garchomp from Dragapult’s guaranteed Draco Meteor KO while Icy Wind slows both foes, letting Garchomp move ahead of Dragapult next turn and preserving the immediate Stomping Tantrum KO threat on Metagross.
decisions.notebook: Opponent revealed Klefki Light Clay dual screens with Prankster; Rotom-Wash Leftovers with Hydro Pump, Volt Switch, Will-O-Wisp, Protect; Mega Metagross is Jolly and Mega Dragapult is Timid Life Orb. Prioritize speed control against Dragapult before exposing Garchomp to Draco Meteor.

decisions.rationale: Dragapult (213 Speed) outspeeds Garchomp and Draco Meteor is a guaranteed OHKO from 43%. If Garchomp Protects (33% consecutive success), it wastes its turn and Metagross is safe. Either way, Metagross Zen Headbutt pressures Milotic (40–75%) with a chance to KO before Sitrus Berry matters. This line removes Garchomp or forces a low-odds Protect while damaging Milotic, setting up a favourable 2v1 or 2v2 against Floette-Mega next turn.
decisions.notebook: Opponent team: Floette-Mega (Fairy Aura, Modest, Floettite), Garchomp (Rough Skin, Life Orb, Jolly, burned), Milotic (Sitrus Berry, Competitive, Bold), Talonflame (Focus Sash, Gale Wings, Jolly, fainted). Screens from Light Clay Klefki still active. Metagross-Mega is primary win condition under screens; Bullet Punch does 46–89% to Floette-Mega. Dragapult (Life Orb, Timid, 213 Speed) is fastest on field. Rotom-Wash (28%) is only bench. Garchomp burned and Reflect-nerfed; Draco Meteor OHKOs it. Floette-Mega is the opponent's main threat; removing it wins the game.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Hydro Pump has the best chance to immediately remove the 5% Metagross; attempting Protect preserves Garchomp on success and, if it fails into Draco Meteor, brings Floette in safely afterward against a weakened Dragapult.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Klefki carries Light Clay with Prankster dual screens. Rotom-Wash is Leftovers with Hydro Pump, Volt Switch, Will-O-Wisp, and Protect. Metagross is Jolly Mega Metagross; Dragapult is Timid Life Orb. Preserve or establish speed control before leaving Garchomp exposed to Dragapult's Draco Meteor.

decisions.rationale: Dragapult Shadow Ball into Garchomp (30.7–55.2% into 37%) and Rotom Volt Switch into Milotic (27.7–49.4% into 32%) both have solid KO chances while preserving Dragapult's full Special Attack for Floette-Mega. Dragapult is guaranteed to move first and cannot be KO'd this turn even under worst-case double-target (max 78.2% vs 81% HP). If both KOs land, Floette-Mega faces a 2v1 with a full-power Dragapult; if only one KO lands, the 2v2 still features an unboosted Dragapult that threatens Floette-Mega with Shadow Ball. Draco Meteor would guarantee the Garchomp KO but leave Dragapult at –2, crippling its ability to pressure Floette-Mega.
decisions.notebook: Floette-Mega (Fairy Aura, Modest, Floettite) is the opponent's win condition; Moonblast OHKOs both Dragapult and Rotom through Light Screen. Dragapult must preserve Special Attack to have any chance against it. Shadow Ball from full-power Dragapult does 24.3–43% to Floette-Mega; Rotom Hydro Pump does 22.1–38.3%. Combined best-case is ~81%, so Floette-Mega is not a guaranteed one-turn KO even with both attacking. Garchomp's Protect streak is 2 (heavily reduced). Milotic has Competitive; avoid stat drops that trigger it. Screens: Light Screen 3 turns, Reflect 2 turns remaining.

decisions.rationale: Protect Milotic while pivoting Garchomp into Floette-Mega preserves both remaining Pokémon against the immediate Dragapult/Rotom pressure. Floette threatens guaranteed KOs on either foe next turn with Moonblast or Energy Ball.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's Klefki set dual screens with Light Clay and Prankster. Rotom-Wash is Leftovers with Hydro Pump, Volt Switch, Will-O-Wisp, and Protect; Dragapult is Timid Life Orb. Mega Floette's Fairy Aura Moonblast reliably threatens Dragapult, while Energy Ball threatens Rotom-Wash.

decisions.rationale: Floette-Mega Moonblast OHKOs both of my Pokémon through Light Screen. Dragapult Shadow Ball (37.6–63.8%) into Floette followed by Rotom Hydro Pump (32–56.4%) guarantees the KO on Floette even on minimum damage rolls: worst case 69% – 37.6% = 31.4%, and Hydro Pump min 32% finishes it. Dragapult outspeeds Floette, so Shadow Ball lands before Floette moves. Floette will KO Dragapult (unless it targets Rotom), but Rotom then removes Floette. The 80% Hydro Pump accuracy is the only risk; no alternative avoids relying on a prediction that could lose both Pokémon. After this exchange Rotom faces Milotic (32%) and burned Garchomp (37%) with Leftovers recovery, a winnable 1v2 endgame.
decisions.notebook: Floette-Mega is the opponent's sole win condition; it must be eliminated first at any cost. Dragapult Shadow Ball + Rotom Hydro Pump is the only guaranteed double-up that KOs Floette regardless of damage rolls, assuming Hydro Pump hits. After Floette falls, Rotom can clean Milotic and burned Garchomp with Volt Switch and Hydro Pump, aided by Leftovers.

decisions.rationale: Moonblast forces Dragapult to Protect or be KOed, while Icy Wind punishes that line with crucial additional Speed control and chips both foes.
decisions.notebook: Klefki carries Prankster dual screens with Light Clay. Rotom-Wash is Leftovers with Hydro Pump, Volt Switch, Will-O-Wisp, and Protect. Timid Life Orb Dragapult has Shadow Ball, Draco Meteor, U-turn, and Protect. Mega Floette's Fairy Aura Moonblast reliably threatens Dragapult, while Energy Ball reliably threatens Rotom-Wash.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Only Rotom-Wash remains. Both foes outspeed and will attack first, but combined max damage (~29%) cannot KO Rotom from 35% through Light Screen. Volt Switch into Milotic has 100% accuracy and ~80% chance to KO from 32% (27.7–49.4% range). If it KOs, Rotom faces burned Garchomp 1v1 with Leftovers, where Hydro Pump 2HKOs while Rock Slide chips slowly. Hydro Pump on Garchomp is inferior: 80% accuracy and only ~42% net KO odds. Protect stalls but wastes the last turn of Light Screen. Will-O-Wisp is redundant (Garchomp already burned, Milotic is special).
decisions.notebook: Floette-Mega is the opponent's sole win condition; it must be eliminated first at any cost. After Floette falls, Rotom-Wash can clean Milotic and burned Garchomp with Volt Switch and Hydro Pump, aided by Leftovers.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Rotom-Wash for the only immediate KO line before it can guarantee a KO with either Volt Switch or Hydro Pump.
decisions.notebook: Rotom-Wash is Leftovers Levitate with Hydro Pump, Volt Switch, Will-O-Wisp, and Protect; Volt Switch threatens Milotic while Hydro Pump threatens Garchomp. Klefki’s Light Clay screens can extend defensive turns.

decisions.rationale: Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump is a guaranteed OHKO on the 21% burned Garchomp. Garchomp's Rock Slide does 7.6–10.8% (non-crit), leaving Rotom at 2.2–5.4%, so Rotom survives and wins. Even if Garchomp Protects, Rotom can simply Hydro Pump next turn; Garchomp cannot stall forever. No other move is useful: Volt Switch is immune, Will-O-Wisp redundant, and Protect only delays the inevitable. Dragapult is fainted and must pass.
Rock Slide is Garchomp's only damaging legal option against Levitate Rotom-Wash and can secure the final KO.
decisions.notebook: Rotom-Wash is Leftovers Levitate with Hydro Pump, Volt Switch, Will-O-Wisp, and Protect. Preserve Ground attacks for non-Levitate targets; use Rock Slide against Rotom-Wash when Garchomp is the remaining attacker.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp outspeeds and Rock Slide is a guaranteed KO on 6% Rotom. However, Rotom's Protect blocks Rock Slide. Garchomp's other moves (Earthquake, Stomping Tantrum) are Ground-type and Rotom is immune via Levitate. At end of turn, Garchomp's burn deals 1/16 (≈6.25%) of max HP, guaranteed KO from 5%. Rotom's Protect has reset since its last use on turn 2, so it works at full reliability. This is a guaranteed win.
Rock Slide is Garchomp's only available damaging option against Levitate Rotom-Wash and can end the game immediately before Rotom moves.

reflections.summary: We won because Klefki set dual screens early, letting Rotom-Wash survive Floette-Mega’s Energy Ball and Metagross soak Ground hits. Will-O-Wisp burned Garchomp, and Leftovers gave Rotom-Wash sustain. Dragapult’s Shadow Ball and Rotom’s Hydro Pump eliminated Floette, the opponent’s sole win condition, after which Rotom-Wash stalled the weakened Garchomp for the win.
reflections.adjustment: Next game expect a different lead to protect Floette, possibly with Scrafty’s Fake Out. Lead Dragapult to threaten Floette immediately with Shadow Ball, or bring your own Scrafty for Fake Out and Intimidate against Garchomp. Keep Rotom-Wash healthy by avoiding early Grass hits.
reflections.notebook: Floette-Mega is the opponent’s sole win condition; eliminate it at any cost. Opponent leads aggressively with Floette + Garchomp, often double‑Protecting Garchomp to stall. Garchomp spams Stomping Tantrum after failed moves; burn cripples it. Milotic runs Icy Wind for speed control, Hydro Pump, and Sitrus Berry; it can surprise with special bulk. Talonflame has Focus Sash and Tailwind but dies to strong Electric moves before Sash activates. Opponent did not bring Scrafty or Goodra this game but may bring Scrafty for Fake Out and Intimidate next game—prepare Fairy countermeasures. Rotom-Wash cleans late‑game with Leftovers, especially if Garchomp is burned. Screens from Klefki are valuable but draw early pressure; apply Thunder Wave before it faints if possible.

reflections.summary: Lost because Rotom-Wash survived repeated low-HP situations, burned Garchomp, and then used Leftovers plus Protect to outlast the final 1v1. The Floette/Garchomp/Milotic core and Mega Floette were suitable into Dragapult and Metagross, but Talonflame was removed before providing Tailwind or meaningful pressure.
reflections.adjustment: Prioritize securing Rotom-Wash’s knockout before committing Garchomp to a burn-sensitive endgame; preserve Floette or Milotic pressure on Rotom rather than relying on burned Life Orb Garchomp to finish it.
reflections.notebook: Opponent led Klefki + Rotom-Wash and used Prankster Reflect/Light Screen support before bringing Mega Metagross and Life Orb Dragapult; Incineroar and Corviknight were not brought. Respect early dual screens and Rotom-Wash’s Will-O-Wisp, Protect, and Leftovers endgame; keep a special attacker available to conclusively remove Rotom-Wash.
